title: CHAPTER NINETEEN. Christian liberty: definition
latin: CAPUT DECIMUM NONUM, De libertate Christiana. Libertas Christiana est fructus plenitudinis gratiae et veritatis quae per Christum facta est, qua fideles a servitute peccati, legis damnatoriae, et caerimoniarum Mosaicarum liberati, in libertatem filiorum Dei vocati, rebus adiaphoris libere utuntur ad aedificationem.
english: Christian liberty is the fruit of the fullness of grace and truth that came through Christ, by which believers, freed from bondage to sin, the condemning law, and Mosaic ceremonies, called into the liberty of God's children, freely use indifferent things for edification.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Christian liberty stands as ye fruit belonging toward ye fullness belonging toward grace and truth that came through Christ, by which believers, freed from bondage toward sin, ye condemning law, and Mosaic ceremonies, called into ye liberty belonging toward God's children, freely use indifferent things for edification. — CHAPTER NINETEEN. On Christian liberty.

title: Freedom from sin and from the law's curse
latin: Libertas a servitute peccati est regeneratio et sanctificatio, qua peccatum non dominatur (Rom. 6). Libertas a lege est a maledictione et rigoroso iure legis quoad iustificationem—non a norma morali. Ceremoniae Mosaicae abrogatae sunt in Christo; forenses determinationes iuris singularis populi Iudaici Christianos non adstringunt quatenus particulares.
english: Freedom from sin's bondage is regeneration and sanctification, so that sin does not reign (Rom. 6). Freedom from the law is from its curse and rigorous right as to justification—not from the moral norm.
Mosaic ceremonies are abrogated in Christ; forensic determinations of Jewish particular law do not bind Christians insofar as they are particular.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Mosaic ceremonies stand as abrogated in Christ; forensic determinations belonging toward Jewish particular law do not bind Christians insofar as they stand as particular. — Freedom from sin's bondage stands as regeneration and sanctification, so that sin does not reign (Rom. 6). Freedom from ye law stands as from its curse and rigorous right as toward justification—not from ye moral norm.

title: Indifferent things; abuse; magistrate and Mosaic forensics
latin: In rebus indifferentibus libertas non extenditur ad scandalum infirmorum nec ad necessitatis cultum rebus adiaphoris affingendum. Gravissime peccant qui rebus indifferentibus necessitatis cultum affingunt, vel res adiaphoras esse fingunt quae minime sunt. Christiani non obligantur legibus forensibus Mosis quatenus ius singulare; quod morale in iis manet. Improbandi Carlostadius et Monetarius qui magistratum Christianum necessitati legum particularium forensium Mosis alligarunt (contra Lutherum, Melanchthonem, Calvinum).
english: In indifferent things liberty does not extend to scandalizing the weak nor to fastening a worship of necessity on adiaphora. Those err most gravely who attach necessary worship to indifferent things, or pretend things are indifferent that are not.

Christians are not bound by Moses' forensic laws as particular right; what is moral in them remains. Carlstadt and Müntzer are rejected for binding the Christian magistrate to Moses' particular forensic laws.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Christians stand as not bound by Moses' forensic laws as particular right; what stands as moral in them remains. Carlstadt and Müntzer stand as rejected for binding ye Christian magistrate toward Moses' particular forensic laws. — In indifferent things liberty does not extend toward scandalizing ye weak nor toward fastening a worship belonging toward necessity on adiaphora. Those err most gravely who attach necessary worship toward indifferent things, or pretend things stand as indifferent that stand as not.

title: Consequences: sonship; Spirit of adoption; Cap.20 next
latin: X. Consequens libertatis e servitute peccati et legis, cui pax conscientiae annectitur, est tum ius filiorum Dei, tum missio Spiritus adoptionis in corda fidelium. XI. Ius filiorum Dei est quod constituti sunt heredes Dei et cohaeredes Christi—etiam liberatio corporum a vanitate (Rom. 8:15-23). XII. Missio Spiritus adoptionis nos certos reddit gloriae futurae. CAPUT VIGESIMUM sequitur, De militia et cruce Christiana.
english: X. A consequence of liberty from sin and law—to which peace of conscience is annexed—is both the right of God's children and the sending of the Spirit of adoption into believers' hearts.
XI–XII. The right of sons is that they are heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, including the body's liberation from vanity; the Spirit of adoption assures us of coming glory.
CHAPTER TWENTY follows, On Christian warfare and the cross.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY follows, On Christian warfare and ye cross. — XI–XII. Ye right belonging toward sons stands as that they stand as heirs belonging toward God and co-heirs with Christ, including ye body's liberation from vanity; ye Spirit belonging toward adoption assures us belonging toward coming glory. — X. A consequence belonging toward liberty from sin and law—to which peace belonging toward conscience stands as annexed—is both ye right belonging toward God's children and ye sending belonging toward ye Spirit belonging toward adoption into believers' hearts.
